process_area.title: Corporate Security Strategy, Threat Intelligence & Risk Framework

value_stream.name: Corporate Security, Executive Protection & Travel Risk Management

fields.Owner: Chief Security Officer (CSO) / Head of Corporate Security
fields.Participants: CEO, CFO, Head of Internal Audit & Risk (VS-21.2), VP Legal (VS-100.3), Board Risk Committee (VS-36), Insurance (VS-26)
fields.Trigger: Enterprise risk strategy (VS-33/VS-21.2); board direction; annual review

workflows.name: Corporate Security Strategy, Charter & Risk-Appetite Framework

Automation Opportunity: - Risk-appetite dashboard; charter/RACI workflow linking adjacent security/risk functions
Controls: - CTL-707: charter board-endorsed (VS-36); explicit RACI vs. LP/HSE/cyber; risk-appetite documented (VS-21.2)
Cross-references: - links to VS-33/VS-21.2 (strategy/ERM), VS-36 (board), VS-26 (BCP/insurance), VS-23/VS-24/VS-27.3 (adjacent security functions)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Charter-ambiguity risk**: Unclear CSO authority/scope vs. LP (VS-23), HSE (VS-24), cyber (VS-27.3) → gaps/overlaps in a crisis; mitigated by an explicit charter and RACI with adjacent functions
- **Under-resourcing risk**: Program funded only after an incident; mitigated by board-endorsed risk-appetite and quantified exposure
System Touchpoints: - ERM/risk register (VS-21.2); board governance (VS-36); insurance/K&R (VS-26); policy management (VS-88)

steps.activity: Set the corporate-security strategy and charter: mission, scope (people, principals, assets, reputation), governance (CSO reporting line — typically to CEO/Head of Internal Audit & Risk/VP Legal & Compliance), and the risk-appetite for intentional-human-threat exposure (executive protection, travel, investigations)
steps.r: CSO / Head of Internal Audit & Risk / VP Legal

steps.activity: Align the strategy to enterprise risk management (VS-21.2 W122) and BCP (VS-26); define the corporate-security risk taxonomy (protective, travel, investigative, workplace-violence, civil-unrest, kidnap/extortion, convergence with cyber VS-27.3) and KRIs
steps.r: CSO / Head of Internal Audit & Risk

steps.activity: Obtain board/risk-committee endorsement (VS-36); fund the program (CSO headcount, GSOC, vendors, insurance — links VS-26 K&R cover); publish the policy enterprise-wide

fields.Participants: HR (VS-19/VS-84), LP (VS-23), Ethics (VS-119), Legal (VS-100.3), law-enforcement liaison
fields.Trigger: Threat indicator; pre-event/pre-travel; periodic principal review; tip from HR/LP/ethics
fields.Volume: ~dozens of assessments/yr (events, travel, principals, disgruntled-employee flags)

Automation Opportunity: - Cross-function threat-indicator intake; OSINT/social-media alerting; case-management workflow
Controls: - CTL-707 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Security Strategy, Threat Intelligence & Risk Framework (PA-159.1).)
- CTL-707: assessments documented and evidence-based; Legal/privacy-compliant (VS-91/VS-100.3); law-enforcement referral where warranted
Cross-references: - links to VS-19/VS-84/VS-150 (HR/labor/drug-free), VS-23 (LP), VS-119 (ethics), VS-91/VS-100.3 (privacy/legal), W4675 (OSINT), W4678 (principal profile)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Late-intelligence risk**: A credible threat detected only after it materializes; mitigated by continuous monitoring + cross-function intake
- **Privacy/defamation risk**: Threat assessment on an individual breaching privacy (VS-91) or defaming; mitigated by Legal review and documented, evidence-based process
System Touchpoints: - Case/threat-assessment system (security ops); HR/LP/ethics feeds (VS-19/VS-23/VS-119); OSINT/HUMINT tools (W4675); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Operate the protective-intelligence function: intake threat indicators (from OSINT/HUMINT W4675, HR disgruntled-employee flags VS-84/VS-150, LP VS-23, ethics hotline VS-119, social-media monitoring); triage and assess credibility, capability, and proximity

Conduct threat assessments for principals (W4678), high-risk events (W4684), and pre-travel (W4687); assign a threat level and recommend protective posture (enhanced EP, route change, event cancellation, law-enforcement referral)
Document each assessment and decision; coordinate with Legal (defamation/privacy limits VS-91/VS-100.3) and law enforcement (PNP/NBI) where a credible threat warrants; close and review the case

fields.Participants: CSO, Legal (VS-100.3), Privacy (VS-91), external intelligence provider
fields.Volume: ~25–40 monitored entities (10–20 principal names per W4678, brand/trademark terms, key executives, regions, sourcing destinations)

Automation Opportunity: - OSINT/dark-web monitoring platform; alert-correlation engine; privacy-scoping rules
Controls: - CTL-707: monitoring lawful and privacy-compliant (VS-91/VS-100.3); alerts triaged and escalated; intelligence retained per policy
Cross-references: - links to W4674 (protective intel), VS-27.3 W397 (cyber intel), VS-122 (sourcing destinations), VS-91/VS-100.3 (privacy/legal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Alert-fatigue risk**: High OSINT volume → real threats missed in noise; mitigated by tuned thresholds and correlation
- **Over-collection/legal risk**: Monitoring exceeding lawful/privacy bounds → liability (VS-91); mitigated by Legal/Privacy governance and public-source scoping
System Touchpoints: - OSINT/social-media monitoring platform; cyber threat intel (VS-27.3 W397); security ops case system; records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Operate OSINT monitoring (news, social media, dark-web mentions of principals, brand, threats, protests near sites/HQ, geopolitical events in sourcing destinations VS-122); HUMINT via vetted sources and the guard force (W4677)
Triage alerts: filter noise, escalate credible indicators to protective intelligence (W4674); correlate with internal indicators (HR, LP, cyber VS-27.3 W397) for converged threats
Govern monitoring within privacy/legal limits (VS-91/VS-100.3 — monitoring public OSINT, not unlawful surveillance); retain intelligence per policy (VS-88)

fields.Participants: LP (VS-23), Facilities (VS-138), IT/cyber (VS-27.3), BCP (VS-26), guard force (W4677)
fields.Volume: 1 GSOC; ~ monitoring of sites, travel, intelligence, alarms across 200 stores + 4 DCs + HQ + travelers

workflows.name: Corporate Security Operations Center (GSOC) — 24/7 Monitoring & Coordination

Automation Opportunity: - Integrated GSOC platform (alarm/CCTV/traveler/intel); automated dispatch; incident-command workflow
Controls: - CTL-707: 24/7 staffing; integrated monitoring; incident-command RACI; every incident logged
Cross-references: - links to W4673 (charter), W4675 (intel), W4687/W4688 (travel), VS-23/VS-27.3/VS-26 (adjacent incident functions), W4696 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Coverage-gap risk**: A GSOC that doesn't run 24/7 or doesn't integrate traveler/intel feeds misses the window to intervene; mitigated by 24/7 staffing and integrated monitoring
- **Handoff-confusion risk**: Unclear incident-command handoff across corporate-security/LP/cyber/BCP; mitigated by the charter RACI (W4673)
System Touchpoints: - GSOC platform (alarm/CCTV/traveler/integration); LP systems (VS-23); cyber SOC (VS-27.3); BCP (VS-26); case management (W4696)

steps.activity: Operate the GSOC 24/7: monitor site alarms/CCTV (VS-23/VS-71), traveler location (W4687/W4688), intelligence feeds (W4675), and incident channels; triage and dispatch response (guard, LP, law enforcement, medical)

Coordinate response across functions: corporate-security incidents, site incidents (VS-23/VS-147), cyber incidents (VS-27.3 W383), BCP events (VS-26); maintain the incident command role until handoff (for BCP-class events the handoff lands on the W848 Crisis Management Team per the [Event Custody & Precedence Register](../event-custody-and-precedence-register.md) §3)
Log every incident, response, and outcome in the case system; produce daily/weekly intelligence & incident summaries for CSO/leadership; feed trend analysis (W4696)

fields.Frequency: Per new site + periodic standard refresh
fields.Participants: Facilities (VS-138), Store Ops (VS-07), LP (VS-23), guard agencies (W4680)
fields.Trigger: New site/building (VS-37/VS-138); standard refresh; audit finding
fields.Volume: ~205 sites (200 stores + 4 DCs + HQ) + executive residences/events

workflows.name: Physical Security Architecture, Access Control & Guard-Force Standards (Enterprise)

Automation Opportunity: - Enterprise access-control/CCTV aggregation; visitor-management automation; guard-tour verification
Controls: - CTL-707: enterprise physical-security standards; guard-force vetting/training; assured via VS-21.3 W358
Cross-references: - distinct from VS-07 W71/VS-04 W797 (site-level); links to VS-138 (facilities), VS-21.3 W358 (audit), W4680 (guard agencies)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fragmented-platforms risk**: Each site on a different access-control/CCTV system → no enterprise visibility; mitigated by the enterprise platform standard
- **Guard-quality risk**: Under-trained/vetted guards ineffective in a crisis; mitigated by guard-force standards and agency oversight (W4680)
System Touchpoints: - Enterprise access-control/CCTV platform; visitor management; guard-force management; facilities (VS-138); LP systems (VS-23)
Time Estimate: - ~per standard refresh 1–2 weeks; per new site ~1–3 days application

steps.activity: Set enterprise physical-security standards (access-control system, CCTV coverage and retention, perimeter, intrusion detection, visitor management) for HQ/executive sites above the store/DC baseline (VS-07 W71/VS-04 W797); govern the enterprise access-control/CCTV platform
Set guard-force standards (posting, training, arming posture, command-and-control, vetting); define the guard agency SLA and oversight (W4680); coordinate guard response with the GSOC (W4676)
Apply standards to new sites (VS-37 store opening / VS-138 facilities) and refresh at existing sites; assure via VS-21.3 W358 physical-security audit

fields.Participants: Protective Intelligence (W4674), Legal (VS-100.3), Insurance (VS-26 K&R), principals' offices
fields.Trigger: Principal change; quarterly review; threat indicator

workflows.name: Executive & Principal Threat Profile, Risk Register & Quarterly Review

Automation Opportunity: - Profile-change/event-trigger review; principal-risk-register integration with ERM; access-controlled profile repository
Controls: - CTL-707: profiles reviewed quarterly + on event; K&R coverage adequacy assessed; principal data privacy-governed (VS-91)
Cross-references: - links to W4674 (protective intel), VS-21.2 (ERM), VS-26 (K&R insurance), VS-91/VS-100.3 (privacy/legal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Static-profile risk**: A profile not updated after a threat-attracting event (e.g., a controversial business decision) → under-protection; mitigated by quarterly + event-triggered review
- **Privacy risk**: Principal profile data mishandled; mitigated by tight access and VS-91 governance
System Touchpoints: - Principal-profile system (security ops); ERM (VS-21.2); K&R insurance (VS-26); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Maintain a threat profile per principal (exposure from role, wealth, public profile, travel, family, residence, recent events/decisions that could attract threat); set the baseline protective posture
Maintain the principal-risk register entry in the ERM (VS-21.2); review quarterly with the Head of Internal Audit & Risk and principals' offices; adjust posture on threat change
steps.r: CSO / Head of Internal Audit & Risk

steps.activity: Coordinate K&R insurance coverage adequacy (VS-26), privacy of principal data (VS-91), and Legal liaison (VS-100.3) for any threat-related matter

workflows.name: Travel Risk Intelligence, Geopolitical & Kidnap/Extortion Monitoring

Automation Opportunity: - Destination-risk feed into travel-booking; active-trip geo-alerting; K&R-readiness checklist
Controls: - CTL-707: destination intelligence continuously refreshed; high-risk trips assessed and briefed; K&R response readiness maintained
Cross-references: - links to W4686/W4687/W4688 (K&R/travel), VS-26 (K&R insurance), VS-81 (CIT), VS-122 (sourcing destinations), VS-160 (mobility)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stale-intelligence risk**: Destination risk not updated (e.g., a sudden civil-unrest event) → traveler exposed; mitigated by continuous monitoring + active-trip alerting
- **Kidnap-response-unreadiness risk**: A kidnap/extortion incident with no rehearsed response → catastrophic outcome; mitigated by W4686 protocol and K&R cover (VS-26)
System Touchpoints: - Destination-risk intelligence platform; traveler-tracking (W4687); GSOC (W4676); K&R insurance (VS-26); mobility (VS-160)

steps.activity: Maintain destination-risk intelligence (crime, kidnap, civil-unrest, terrorism, health, natural-disaster ratings) for domestic Philippine regions and international sourcing destinations; refresh continuously

For each high-risk trip (executive travel, cash-carrying VS-81, sourcing to elevated-risk destinations), produce a travel-risk assessment and recommend posture (route/lodging, EP support, tracking, avoidance); brief the traveler (W4687)
Monitor active-trip travelers for emerging threats (W4676 GSOC); maintain K&R/extortion response readiness (W4686) and feed travel-risk into mobility policy (VS-160)

fields.Trigger: Vendor selection/renewal; performance issue; TPRM review (VS-161)
fields.Volume: ~8–15 security vendors (guard agencies, EP providers, intelligence providers, investigation firms, K&R consultant)

workflows.name: Corporate Security Vendor, Guard-Agency & Investigator Management

Automation Opportunity: - Vendor-licensure/insurance tracking; SLA dashboards; TPRM integration (VS-161)
Controls: - CTL-707 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Security Strategy, Threat Intelligence & Risk Framework (PA-159.1).)
- CTL-707: vendors licensed/vetted (VS-161); SLA-managed; confidentiality and conduct assured (VS-86/VS-91/VS-119)
Cross-references: - links to VS-34/VS-03 (procurement), VS-161 (TPRM), VS-67 (scorecard), VS-100.3/VS-86/VS-91/VS-119 (legal/ABC/privacy/ethics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unlicensed/unvetted-vendor risk**: A guard/EP/investigation vendor without proper licensure/vetting → liability and ineffective protection; mitigated by TPRM due diligence (VS-161)
- **Confidentiality-breach risk**: A security vendor mishandling principal/investigation data; mitigated by confidentiality contracts and VS-91 data-handling
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/vendor (VS-34/VS-03); TPRM (VS-161); vendor scorecard (VS-67); contracts (VS-100.3); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Select and contract corporate-security vendors (guard agencies, EP providers, intelligence/investigation firms) via procurement (VS-34) and TPRM due diligence (VS-161): licensure (PNP-SOSIA for security agencies), vetting, insurance, confidentiality

Govern vendor performance against SLA (guard quality, EP responsiveness, intelligence timeliness); manage the lifecycle (renewal/exit per VS-67/VS-161); enforce confidentiality and data-handling (VS-91)
Assure vendor conduct (no rights-abuses, no corruption — links VS-86/VS-119); manage conflicts of interest and sole-source justification for sensitive services
